LESSON: READING 4.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – POETRY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should there be security measures in school?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to questions from texts for information
2. create a glossary with words related to the theme for information
3. construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication
4. appreciate the role of reading as a way of acquiring information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – POETRY
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION – POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Respond to questions from texts for information

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to questions from texts for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to questions from texts for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to questions from texts for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a glossary with words related to the theme for information

What this means
In this part you learn to create a glossary with words related to the theme for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a glossary with words related to the theme for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a glossary with words related to the theme for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the role of reading as a way of acquiring information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of reading as a way of acquiring information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of reading as a way of acquiring information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of reading as a way of acquiring information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to questions from texts for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry to a partner. (skill: create a glossary with words related to the theme for information)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the role of reading as a way of acquiring information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to questions from texts for information.
3. Practise this skill: create a glossary with words related to the theme for information.
4. Practise this skill: construct sentences using the new vocabulary for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should there be security measures in school?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Reading for information – Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to questions from texts for information.
5. Be able to: create a glossary with words related to the theme for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
